summary: This project focuses on developing a high-precision closed-loop 6 Degrees of Freedom (DOF) control system for antenna positioning used in satellite and aerospace applications. The solution enables accurate spatial orientation and trajectory control using real-time feedback and advanced kinematic modeling. It significantly improves positioning reliability for critical communication and space operations.

challenge.description: The aerospace industry demands extremely precise control systems for spacecraft orientation and antenna positioning, where even minor deviations can lead to mission-critical failures. Existing systems face challenges in integrating multiple technologies such as stepper motors, laser tracking, and AI-based control while maintaining synchronization and accuracy. Additionally, achieving high reliability with cost efficiency in satellite-grade systems remains a major constraint, requiring robust closed-loop control and real-time validation mechanisms.

methodology.title: System Design & Hardware Integration
methodology.description: Designed and integrated stepper motors, drivers, and Arduino UNO to build the foundational closed-loop actuation system for 6DOF antenna movement control.

methodology.title: Kinematics & Trajectory Planning
methodology.description: Developed inverse kinematics models and trajectory planning algorithms in MATLAB to compute precise antenna orientation and motion paths in 3D space.

methodology.title: Real-Time Feedback & Validation
methodology.description: Implemented Laser Tracker and PolyWorks integration for real-time measurement, validation, and correction of antenna positioning to ensure micron-level accuracy.

impact.label: POSITIONING ACCURACY
impact.description: Achieved extremely high precision in antenna positioning through closed-loop feedback and real-time correction systems.

impact.label: FEEDBACK SYSTEM
impact.description: Enabled continuous monitoring and validation using Laser Tracker and PolyWorks for improved system reliability.

impact.label: MANUAL INTERVENTION
impact.description: Automation of control and correction loops significantly minimized human intervention in antenna alignment operations.
